    # Must be a regular file (not symlink, not directory)
    [[ -f "$f" && ! -L "$f" ]] || continue
    candidates+=("$f")
done

# If no candidates, nothing to do
if [[ ${#candidates[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    exit 0
fi

# Extract timestamp from each filename and sort by timestamp (oldest first)
# Format: PREFIX-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS.tar.gz
# We need to extract YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS part

declare -a sorted_files=()
declare -a timestamps=()

# Create an array of "timestamp<TAB>filepath" and sort by timestamp
tmp_list="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp_list"' EXIT

for f in "${candidates[@]}"; do
    base="$(basename "$f")"
    # Extract the timestamp part: after the prefix- and before .tar.gz
    # The name is: PREFIX-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS.tar.gz
    # We know the prefix, so we can strip it
    # Remove the leading dir path to get basename
    # base = PREFIX-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS.tar.gz
    # Strip "PREFIX-" from front and ".tar.gz" from back
    ts="${base#"$prefix"-}"   # remove prefix-
    ts="${ts%.tar.gz}"        # remove .tar.gz
    timestamps+=("$ts")
    printf '%s\t%s\n' "$ts" "$f" >> "$tmp_list"
done

# Sort by timestamp (oldest first) - timestamps are in YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS format which sorts lexicographically
sorted_files=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r ts filepath; do
    sorted_files+=("$filepath")
done < <(sort -t$'\t' -k1,1 "$tmp_list")

# Total count:
total=${#sorted_files[@]}

# Determine which files to keep:
# 1. The KEEP newest backups (last $keep in the sorted array)
# 2. Additionally, the newest backup of each of the last 4 calendar months that have backups

# Mark files to keep using an associative array by filepath
declare -A to_keep=()

# Keep the last $keep files (newest)
if [[ $total -gt $keep ]]; then
    start=$(( total - keep ))
else
    start=0
fi
for ((i=start; i<total; i++)); do
    to_keep["${sorted_files[$i]}"]=1
done

# Now handle the "last 4 calendar months" rule.
# For each of the last 4 distinct calendar months (YYYYmm) that appear in the sorted list,
# keep the newest backup from that month.
# "Last 4 calendar months that have backups" means: look at all months present, take the most recent 4 distinct months.

# Extract all YYYYmm values from the timestamps
declare -a months_present=()
declare -A month_seen=()

for ((i=total-1; i>=0; i--)); do
    filepath="${sorted_files[$i]}"
    base="$(basename "$filepath")"
    ts="${base#"$prefix"-}"
    ts="${ts%.tar.gz}"
    yymm="${ts:0:6}"  # YYYYmm
    if [[ -z "${month_seen[$yymm]:-}" ]]; then
        month_seen["$yymm"]=1
        months_present+=("$yymm")
    fi

# months_present is in order from newest to oldest (since we iterated from newest)
# Take the first 4 (or fewer if less than 4 distinct months)
num_months=${#months_present[@]}
if [[ $num_months -gt 4 ]]; then
    num_months=4
fi

for ((mi=0; mi<num_months; mi++)); do
    yymm="${months_present[$mi]}"
    # Find the newest backup in this month (first occurrence when scanning from newest)
    for ((i=total-1; i>=0; i--)); do
        filepath="${sorted_files[$i]}"
        base="$(basename "$filepath")"
        ts="${base#"$prefix"-}"
        ts="${ts%.tar.gz}"
        file_yymm="${ts:0:6}"
        if [[ "$file_yymm" == "$yymm" ]]; then
            to_keep["$filepath"]=1
            break
        fi
    done
done

# Now determine files to delete: all candidates not in to_keep, in oldest-first order
declare -a to_delete=()
for ((i=0; i<total; i++)); do
    filepath="${sorted_files[$i]}"
    if [[ -z "${to_keep[$filepath]:-}" ]]; then
        to_delete+=("$filepath")
    fi
done

for filepath in "${to_delete[@]}"; do
    base="$(basename "$filepath")"
    echo "delete $base"
    if [[ $dry_run -eq 0 ]]; then
        rm -- "$filepath"
    fi
done
